episodes.title: The Water That Would Stop Bullets: Uganda's Yakan "Allah Water" Cult, 1919
episodes.description:
In 1919, in the hills of West Nile on the Uganda–Congo–Sudan frontier, Lugbara men drilled in forest clearings with rifles made of reeds. They had drunk the water of Yakan, sold by a Kakwa prophet named Rembe, and they believed British bullets would turn to water. The water was laced with kamiojo, "lion's medicine". It promised to raise the ancestors and the dead cattle, end taxes, and turn the guns of strangers harmless. This film follows the sacred water from the Sudan to Lugbaraland, through its temples, passwords and parades, to the 1919 rising, the deportation of chiefs and Rembe's hanging at Yei.

This film describes beliefs with respect. Images are illustrative reconstructions; no photographs of anyone involved exist or are used.

Notes:
- The 1890s battle against Emin Pasha's soldiers is Lugbara tradition as reported by Driberg.
- Driberg linked Yakan to the Maji Maji war; later scholars doubt any connection.

Sources:
- J. H. Driberg, "Yakan", Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute 61 (1931): 413-420
- John Middleton, "The Yakan or Allah Water Cult Among the Lugbara", JRAI 93 (1963): 80-108
- Anne King, "The Yakan Cult and Lugbara Response to Colonial Rule", Azania 5 (1970): 1-25
- Tim Allen, "Understanding Alice", Africa 61 (1991): 370-399
- Mark Leopold, Inside West Nile (2005); Idi Amin (2021)
